memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "All the curtains around the courtyard were of finely twisted linen. The bases for the posts were bronze. The hooks and bands on the posts were silver, and their tops were overlaid with silver; so all the posts of the courtyard had silver bands." - Exod 38:16-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Sixty posts stood around that courtyard. Every one of them had a bronze base, silver bands, and a silver-covered top.

Not just the corner posts. Not just the ones by the entrance. All of them.

This is God's consistency on display. He did not decorate the visible posts and leave the ones at the back plain. Each received the same care, the same silver, the same attention.

That says something about how God treats His people. He is not partial. Peter had to learn this and said so plainly: God does not show favouritism, but accepts from every nation the one who fears Him and does what is right (Acts 10:34-35).

We are constantly ranked in this life — by income, appearance, achievement, usefulness. God's courtyard was not built that way.

Notice also the material. Silver again, from the ransom money. Every post capped with redemption. Whatever position a post occupied, its covering came from the same source.

That is exactly true of the church. There is one Lord, one faith, one baptism (Eph 4:5). The mature believer and the newest convert are covered by the same ransom.

Do you treat people the way God built His courtyard?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you rank people in ways God does not?
2. Have you assumed you matter less than more visible believers?
3. Who in your church have you overlooked because they are not prominent?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You show no favouritism. Free me from ranking myself and others, and let me see people as You do. Amen.
